title: UK Biobank adds immune and brain health layers - Nature Biotechnology
text:
The UK Biobank is adding a detailed immune dataset to its repository to enable a better understanding of how immune variation affects health, aging and disease. The collaboration with London-based IMU Biosciences, supported by a £1.57 million ($2.10 million) grant from Sovereign AI, will apply advanced immune-cell profiling, transcriptomic analysis and AI-driven computational methods to blood samples from 80,000 participants to build a comprehensive, population-scale immune dataset. And in October, the UK Biobank announced a study to analyze 80,000 samples for neurodegenerative research. The study, funded by Alzheimer’s Research UK and LifeArc, will use Alamar Biosciences’ proteomics platform to detect low-abundance protein signals that may predict Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases and other neurodegenerative conditions, potentially decades before symptoms emerge.The immune project expects to generate over 100 million data points from each 2-ml blood sample, which will be integrated into a single-cell immune profiling AI foundational dataset. The study will apply IMU’s immune profiling platform combined with Becton Dickinson’s flow cytometry analyzer, Waters’ single-cell multi-omics instrumentation and Ultima Genomics’ next-generation sequencers to assess around 2,500 distinct immune cell subsets in real time. The resulting data will be added to the UK Biobank and made available to approved researchers worldwide.
